chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Sadaqah, from Salih al-Nili, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, is like the one who performed Hajj one hundred times with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition to highlight the unique status of Karbala as a spiritual axis, where 'knowing his right' (Irfan bi-haqqihi) implies recognizing Imam Husayn’s role in preserving the Prophet’s message. This equivalence to a hundred Hajjs underscores the concept of Ziyarah as an act of worship that carries the weight of pilgrimage, particularly emphasized in Shia jurisprudence as a means of drawing closer to God through the Ahl al-Bayt.
